bibliography.note: Crossref: Turesson, H.; Brönmark, C. (2004). Foraging behaviour and capture success in perch, pikeperch and pike and the effects of prey density. Journal of Fish Biology 65(2): 363-375. Matches the reference entry. Title page not seen

claims.claim: northern pike 182–221 mm on roach at 0.30 of pike length: captures per strike 0.15 overall, 0.36 from ambush, 0.12 in pursuit; 2.44-m pools, 19.7 °C, 166 attacks
Eurasian perch 190–235 mm on roach: captures per strike 0.20 on single prey, 0.03 into schools; pools
schooling does not protect against esocids: pike caught roach at the same rate whether single or schooled, while the success of Eurasian perch fell from 0.20 to 0.03
claims.note: check 'rate' (per attack? per unit time?) and the school sizes or prey densities compared

claims.claim: an esocid meets a school as n^0.65 fish at undiminished success (code: 'it finds a school about as it finds one big fish and takes one fish an attack, its success unreduced inside it')
claims.note: only 'success unreduced in a school' can come from this source; the exponent 0.65 is presumably the project's (the paper's sentence puts the citation after both). Say so when rewritten

claims.claim: a school cuts a perch-like predator's success to 0.15 (code: 'perch-like × 0.15 into a school')
claims.note: not cited to this source in §4.5, but it matches 0.03 / 0.20 = 0.15 from the perch row above (project arithmetic, if those values hold). In the code it is a MULTIPLIER (fish3.js:2356: 'cls === 2 ? 0.15'), whereas §4.5 says 'cuts … success to 0.15', which reads as an absolute success

claims.claim: esocids catch as well in schools as singly (Turesson & Brönmark 2004); perch and bass are confused by schools
claims.note: only the pike and perch parts can come from this source (no bass were tested, by its title)

claims.claim: CS3's spiny-rayed value for an esocid was measured at a prey/predator length ratio of ~0.3 ('pike ambush 0.36 at ~0.30, Turesson & Brönmark 2004')
claims.note: roach are soft-rayed cyprinids, not spiny-rayed, so the ratio at which a pike's success on roach was measured is not obviously the right anchor for the spiny-rayed column; worth a look once the text is read
